# iliad-025 — review, pass 1 (Iliad 4.364–456)

Edited `units.json` in place by script; `t` and all other keys untouched (checked unit by unit against a copy of the draft). Severity: major = wrong Greek/English or a false claim that misleads; moderate = a false label, cross-reference or punctuation fault, or a repeated line not reused; minor = wording, consistency, precision.

Counts: major 0 · moderate 7 · minor 11.

## Checked and found sound

- Every grammatical label in every note was checked against the form in its line (case, number, tense, mood, voice, elision, augment, dual, tmesis). Apart from the items above all are true.
- Word-placement claims (e.g. 370 genitives with Tydeus, 405 ἡμεῖς repeated at 406, 439 ὄρσε with Ares) and cross-references (368→401; 369→1.201 / 2.7 (iliad-007, ln 5) / 4.312; 424→442; 423/427; 410 speech end; 1.7 half-line; 2.810 half-line; Od. 8.165 formula) hold.
- Greek → `l` word by word, then `l` ↔ `i`: no further errors of case relation, tense, mood or particle. Every packet row was compared to the unit's `l`/`i` (including all stock epithets, κορύσσεται in both similes, ἐπιείκελος, μενεπτόλεμος, δαΐφρων "wise-minded"/"wise-hearted" with the doubt noted).
- Quotation marks: “ on 370, 404, 412 (the three `mark` units, in `l` and `i`); ” on 400 (end of Agamemnon's speech), 410 (Sthenelus), 418 (Diomedes). No speech runs in from iliad-024 (its last unit, 363, ends the speech with ”) and none runs on into part 026. The unit at 368–369 correctly carries none.
- Repeated lines: 364 takes the shipped English of iliad-024 (ln 292) unchanged, as the packet says (the semicolon is the packet's stated choice); 369 follows the packet row (iliad-002 ln 201 with "to him"), note names 1.201, 2.7 and the pronoun change; 411 is built on the Odyssey/Iliad formula as published (iliad-002 ln 148, iliad-024 ln 349, odyssey-034 ln 165) with κρατερὸς Διομήδης; 419 (iliad-016 ln 29), 448 and 446 (odyssey-002/118) agree with published wording as far as the sentence allows.
- Scansion, 4.407: scanned by hand: παυ-ρό-τε | ρον λᾱ | ὸ ἀ-γα | γόνθ’ ὑ-πὸ | τεῖ-χος ἄ | ρει-ον. The short, open ο of λᾱ-ὸ(ν) stands in the long place of foot 3 (the ν goes with the next syllable before ἀγαγόνθ’); no other division gives six feet. The irregularity is real and the note already says so in one sentence, in the right place. No change.
- `p` flags: 364, 401, 411, 419, 422, 446 match the packet's ¶ marks.

## Findings considered and refused

- 4.448 "a great din went up" / 436 "had sprung up": the published unit at 2.810 (iliad-015) ships "had risen" / "rose", but the conventions table (row ὀρυμαγδός · ὀρώρει) fixes "had sprung up" / "went up", and the iliad-015 note itself says the same. The draft follows the table; the mismatch is in iliad-015, not here. Raise with the owner of the table.
- 4.451 "the earth ran with blood": idiomatic and the packet's choice; built from ῥέω + dative αἷμα; "flowed" is in `l`. Kept.
- 4.421 `i` "fear would have taken hold of even a steadfast man": "taken hold of" is common English for εἷλεν, and the note explains the tmesis; no single source phrase. Kept.
- 4.446 "And when indeed" for οἳ δ’ ὅτε δή ῥ’: published parallels (odyssey-002, odyssey-118) differ among themselves ("And when", "And when then"); δή as "indeed" is not forbidden. Kept.
- 4.382 "And when now they had gone off": the published οἳ δ’ ἐπεὶ οὖν (iliad-019, ln 340) has "And they, when now"; the draft's `l` keeps ἐπεὶ οὖν as "when now" and the pronoun is in the next word; no change needed.
- 4.399–400 `i` "the son he fathered is worse": present-tense copula where the Greek has none; a statement about Diomedes as he is. Kept.
- 4.368 note ("waits for its contrast at 401"): μέν is answered at 401's δέ; the contrast is Agamemnon's reviling against Diomedes' silence, as the note at 401 says. Kept.
- 4.365 `l` "among" vs `i` "amid": a trivial difference of register, not of sense. Kept.
- ἀγαγόνθ’ "dual or elided plural, disputed": the dispute is real; the note does not take a side. Kept.

## For the caller

- `new-renderings.md` (drafter's file, not edited): the row for ἐπιπείθεο μύθῳ (4.412) now has a stale `l` ("be obedient to my word"); the unit has "obey my word" because the half-line repeats a line in iliad-006 (ln 565). The Odyssey-shared 4.374b–375 are not mentioned there either.
- Not touched: `sc`, `tr` and every other key.


# iliad-025 — review, pass 2 (glossary and new-renderings)

Checked all 201 novel entries in `gloss.json` and the 18 `__broaden__` entries against the line(s) each form stands in: lemma, case/tense/mood/number, Attic equivalent, homographs, and format (lemma — meaning; parse; typographic ’ only; under 230 characters, longest now 147; no line numbers, backticks or "here"). Mechanical checks: the 201 keys equal `novel-forms.json`; none already in the Iliad glossary; every broadened entry contains the old entry whole. `gloss.json` was edited in place by script (a copy was compared afterwards: exactly 12 novel entries and 1 broadened entry differ; key order unchanged); `units.json` and every `t` untouched.

Counts: major 1 · moderate 5 · minor 9 (13 changes in `gloss.json`: 1 major, 4 moderate, 8 minor; 2 in `new-renderings.md`: 1 moderate, 1 minor).

## gloss.json changes

| entry | severity | what was wrong | what was done |
|---|---|---|---|
| τάρβει (4.388) | major | Parsed as pres. imper. 2 sg., "fear!". It is the imperfect 3 sg. of ταρβέω without the augment (ἔνθ’ οὐδὲ ξεῖνός περ ἐὼν … τάρβει, "Tydeus was not afraid"); the unit note already says so. | `impf. 3 sg., unaugmented (= ἐτάρβει): ’was afraid’`. |
| ἀγαγόνθ’ (4.407) | moderate | Parse gave no number ("masc. nom."), and did not say where the aspiration comes from. | `masc. nom. dual or pl., elided and aspirated before ὑπό (ἀγαγόνθ’ = ἀγαγόντε ’we two’, or ἀγαγόντες)`; the dual-or-plural dispute is kept, as the unit note has it (a plural would be an unusual elision of -ες, but the note leaves it open and the gloss agrees with the note). |
| ἄρειον (4.407) | moderate | "masc. acc. sg., agreeing with a noun": it agrees with τεῖχος, which is neuter. | `neut. acc. sg., agreeing with τεῖχος`. |
| ἐκέλευον (4.380) | moderate | "unaugmented": ἐκέλευον has its augment. | Removed the word. |
| ἐπῄνεον (4.380) | moderate | "unaugmented": ἐπῄνεον has its augment (η), the point is the uncontracted -εον. | `impf. 3 pl., uncontracted (= Attic ἐπῄνουν)`, as the unit note says. |
| ἐτεοκληείης (4.386) | minor | Epic form given with no Attic equivalent, unlike the published Ἡρακληείης entry. | Added `(= Attic -είας)`. Lemma Ἐτεοκληεῖος kept, parallel to the published Ἡρακληεῖος; sense "might of Eteocles = Eteocles himself" is right. |
| χέρεια (4.400) | minor | Parse (masc. acc. sg., = χερείονα; "than himself" with εἷο) is correct; no Attic equivalent given. The "also neut. nom./acc. pl." clause is a true second form (the Odyssey's τὰ χέρεια) and is kept. | Added `Attic χείρονα`. |
| ἔπληντ’ (4.449) | minor | Parse right (3 pl. aor. mid. ἔπληντο of πελάζω, root aorist) but did not name the aorist. | Added `(root aorist ἐπλήμην)`. |
| ἔτρεψε (4.381) | minor | "+ acc." but Zeus's object is not expressed in the line. | Removed `+ acc.`. |
| κασιγνήτη (4.441) | minor | "fem. voc./nom. sg.": no vocative anywhere; it is the nominative in apposition to Ἔρις. | `fem. nom. sg.` |
| ἴδοντο (4.374) | minor | "(= Attic εἶδον)" is the active; the form is a middle aorist, unaugmented. | `(= augmented εἴδοντο)`. |
| πονεύμενον (4.374) | minor | Called "uncontracted"; it is the Ionic -εύ- for -ού- (πονεόμενον → πονεύμενον). | `epic -εύ- (= Attic πονούμενον)`. |
| __broaden__ κάρη (4.443) | minor | Quoted phrase "κάρη ἐστήριξε" reverses the line's word order. | Now `ἐστήριξε κάρη`. Old entry still inside the new one. |

## Findings considered and refused

- Every other novel entry (the rest) checked against its line and left alone: lemma, parse and Attic equivalent right. Particular checks: εἷσαν (aor. of ἵζω, causative "set"), ἔπεφν’ (ἔπεφνε), εἱμένοι (perf. pass. of ἕννυμι, + τά), ἐστρατόωνθ’, ψεύδε’, εὐχόμεθ’, νῶϊ (dual), στεῖλαν (unaugmented, correctly said), ἀμείνω in `n` and χέρεια as accusatives agreeing with υἱόν.
- ἀγαγόνθ’: did not rule for the dual alone, since the unit note leaves the question open; the gloss and the note now agree.
- ἔπληντ’ "mid./pass.": kept, because the note reads it as passive in sense and the form is the middle root aorist; the gloss covers both.
- Broadened entries (γενέσθαι, εἰπεῖν, θήβης, κέλευε, λεχεποίην, λόχον, νεῖκος, οἷσιν, πολέμου, σύν, τόσσον, τὰ, ἀμείνω, ἐγένοντο, ἱερά, ὁμοίϊον, ὥς, κάρη): each new reading fits the line it comes from and keeps the old entry whole. The older senses inside them (e.g. Odyssey contexts in ὁμοίϊον, ἀμείνω) are published and were not touched.
- Known (already published) forms not in `__broaden__` were not re-audited, as the task limits this pass to novel and broadened entries.
